FR-2: Each simulated request must carry a source channel label (text, voicemail, email,\\n104.   social DM, booking form) and render distinctly enough that the operator can tell where\\n105.   it came from.\\n106. - FR-3: No real message transmission, receipt, or third-party channel connection occurs\\n107.   at any point (see Section 9).\\n108. \\n109. ### 4.2 Parsing\\n110. - FR-4: The system must extract, per request, at minimum: customer name, known/new\\n111.   customer flag, trade/job type, urgency signal(s) (explicit keywords like \\\"ASAP,\\\"\\n112.   \\\"emergency,\\\" \\\"leaking,\\\" or inferred from timing language), requested date/time (if\\n113.   present), address/location (if present), and a completeness flag identifying which of\\n114.   the above are missing.\\n115. - FR-5: Parsing failures (e.g., no discernible job type) must not crash the request —\\n116.   the request should still enter the queue, flagged as low-completeness / needs-info.\\n117. \\n118. ### 4.3 Prioritization\\n119. - FR-6: Every request in the queue must have a visible priority score or tier and a\\n120.   rank position relative to other open requests.\\n121. - FR-7: The prioritization must be recalculated whenever a new request arrives or an\\n122.   existing request's data changes (e.g., owner adds missing info).\\n123. - FR-8: The scoring must be explainable — the dashboard must show *why* a request is\\n124.   ranked where it is (see Section 5.6), directly addressing the \\\"why was this\\n125.   prioritized this way\\\" trust/support risk identified in `business-proposal.md` §5.2.\\n126. \\n127. ### 4.4 Follow-Up Suggestion\\n128. - FR-9: Every request that plausibly needs a reply must have an associated suggested\\n129.   message draft, generated based on its parsed fields and completeness/urgency state.\\n130. - FR-10: Drafts must never be sent automatically. The owner must take an explicit action\\n131.   to mark a message as sent (simulated).\\n132. - FR-11: The owner must be able to edit a draft before \\\"sending\\\" it.\\n133. - FR-12: The owner must be able to request an alternative/regenerated draft for the same\\n134.   request.\\n135. \\n136. ### 4.5 Dashboard\\n137. - FR-13: The dashboard must present requests grouped or filterable by state (Section 6).\\n138. - FR-14: The dashboard must support explicit empty, loading, and error states\\n139.   (Section 6.6).\\n140. - FR-15: The dashboard must be usable one-handed / at a glance, consistent with the\\n141.   mobile-first, low-setup expectation from research — no required configuration step\\n142.   before the queue shows value.\\n143. - FR-16: The owner must be able to transition a request between states manually (e.g.,\\n144.   New → Prioritized → Scheduled → Done), independent of the automatic prioritization\\n145.   scoring.\\n146. \\n147. ### 4.6 Seed Data & Demo Control\\n148. - FR-17: The prototype must ship with seed data covering all three trades and a range of\\n149.   message quality (complete, partial, and highly incomplete requests) per Section 7.\\n150. - FR-18: A reset/replay mechanism should exist so the demo can be re-run from a known\\n151.   starting state.\\n152. \\n153. ---\\n154. \\n155. ## 5. Prioritization Logic\\n156. \\n157. Prioritization makes the operators' existing informal mental checklist\\n158. (`customer-research.md` §7) explicit, consistent, and visible. Each request is evaluated\\n159. against five factors. Each factor contributes to a composite score; the composite score\\n160. determines rank order and priority tier. The scoring approach below is intentionally\\n161. simple and explainable rather than a black-box model, per the transparency requirement\\n162. in `business-proposal.md` §5.2.\\n163. \\n164. ### 5.1 Urgency\\n165. - **Signal sources:** explicit keywords (\\\"ASAP,\\\" \\\"emergency,\\\" \\\"today,\\\" \\\"flooding,\\\"\\n166.   \\\"leaking,\\\" \\\"urgent\\\"), requested timing proximity (e.g., \\\"need it tomorrow\\\" vs. \\\"sometime\\n167.   next month\\\"), and channel-implied urgency (a same-day voicemail reads differently than\\n168.   a booking form for three weeks out).\\n169. - **Effect on score:** Higher urgency raises the composite score and can promote a\\n170.   request above older but lower-urgency requests. Urgency is the most volatile factor —\\n171.   it can override recency of arrival.\\n172. - **Caveat modeled from research:** Unverified urgency from an unfamiliar contact (no\\n173.   address, no photo, vague severity — cf. Darnell's Vignette B) should raise urgency\\n174.   score but simultaneously raise a \\\"needs verification\\\" completeness flag, preventing\\n175.   a request from being ranked as top priority purely on unverified alarm language.\\n176. \\n177. ### 5.2 Customer Value\\n178. - **Signal sources:** known/recurring customer flag, relationship tenure/frequency (if\\n179.   present in seed data), and stated loyalty context (e.g., \\\"I know it's short notice but\\n180.   can you squeeze me in\\\").\\n181. - **Effect on score:** Known, recurring, high-value customers receive a positive score\\n182.   boost even absent urgency language, reflecting the research finding that operators\\n183.   implicitly prioritize trusted recurring clients over louder new leads\\n184.   (`customer-research.md` §7, item 6; §5, item 4). New/unknown customers receive a\\n185.   neutral or reduced boost until vetted.\\n186. \\n187. ### 5.3 Scheduling Constraints\\n188. - **Signal sources:** requested date/time vs. existing simulated bookings/calendar slots\\n189.   for that trade's demo calendar.\\n190. - **Effect on score:** A request that conflicts with an already-committed slot is flagged\\n191.   with a conflict indicator and its score is adjusted downward (or clearly marked as\\n192.   \\\"requires displacing another job\\\") rather than silently ranked high — directly\\n193.   countering the \\\"promising a slot before checking the calendar\\\" failure mode\\n194.   (`customer-research.md` §5, item 5; §6). A request with clear, conflict-free\\n195.   availability receives a small positive adjustment reflecting ease of fulfillment.\\n196. \\n197. ### 5.4 Request Completeness\\n198. - **Signal sources:** presence/absence of address, job scope, timing, and\\n199.   trade-specific critical fields (e.g., pet temperament for pet sitters, photo/severity\\n200.   detail for handymen).\\n201. - **Effect on score:** Incomplete requests are not ranked at the very top even if urgent,\\n202.   because they cannot yet be acted on — they are instead flagged **Needs Info** (see\\n203.   Section 6) and the missing fields are itemized. Completeness does not zero out a\\n204.   request's priority; it caps how high a request can rank until clarified, and directly\\n205.   drives what the suggested follow-up message asks for (Section 8).\\n206. \\n207. ### 5.5 Service Fit\\n208. - **Signal sources:** parsed job type vs. the operator's configured/seeded service scope\\n209.   (e.g., a handyman's electrical work outside comfort/license zone; a cleaning request\\n210.   requiring services Maria doesn't offer).\\n211. - **Effect on score:** Poor or unclear service fit reduces score substantially and may\\n212.   route the request toward a \\\"decline/refer out\\\" suggested draft rather than a\\n213.   scheduling draft, regardless of urgency or customer value.\\n214. \\n215. ### 5.6 Composite Scoring & Explainability\\n216. - Each request's dashboard card must show, at minimum, a short breakdown of which\\n217.   factors pushed its rank up or down (e.g., \\\"Urgent language detected,\\\" \\\"Existing\\n218.   client,\\\" \\\"Conflicts with 2pm booking,\\\" \\\"Missing address\\\"). This is a required\\n219.   transparency element, not optional polish — it exists specifically to preempt the\\n220.   \\\"why was this prioritized this way\\\" trust objection identified in the business\",\"timestamp_utc\":\"2026-07-15T02:42:24.1333860+00:00\"}},{\"sequence\":18,\"type\":\"tool.call\",\"payload\":{\"callId\":\"toolu_01EdbirfHr8QmCC62Mr7q9pw\",\"toolName\":\"view\",\"arguments\":{\"path\":\"/local-workspace/7a76b8db3fefcf2a/c1365ba0329a7d92c80f40b50080da1764f074ca/docs/planning/product-spec.md\",\"view_range\":[220,411]},\"timestamp_utc\":\"2026-07-15T02:42:27.5878490+00:00\"}},{\"sequence\":19,\"type\":\"tool.result\",\"payload\":{\"callId\":\"toolu_01EdbirfHr8QmCC62Mr7q9pw\",\"content\":\"220.   \\\"why was this prioritized this way\\\" trust objection identified in the business\\n221.   proposal.\\n222. - Priority tiers (for dashboard grouping) should be derived from score bands, e.g.\\n223.   **High / Medium / Low**, with **Needs Info** treated as an overlay flag that can apply\\n224.   to a request at any tier rather than a competing tier.\\n225. \\n226. ---\\n227. \\n228. ## 6. Dashboard States\\n229. \\n230. ### 6.1 New\\n231. Request has been parsed but not yet reviewed by the owner. Newly arrived (simulated)\\n232. requests default here before prioritization scoring is applied or immediately alongside\\n233. it.\\n234. \\n235. ### 6.2 Prioritized\\n236. Request has been scored and ranked; sits in the active queue ordered by composite score\\n237. within its tier (High/Medium/Low). This is the default \\\"working\\\" state for actionable\\n238. requests.\\n239. \\n240. ### 6.3 Needs Info\\n241. Overlay/flag state (may apply within New or Prioritized) indicating one or more required\\n242. fields are missing (address, scope, timing, trade-specific detail). Dashboard must\\n243. visually distinguish these from fully actionable requests and surface the specific\\n244. missing fields.\\n245. \\n246. ### 6.4 Scheduled\\n247. Owner has confirmed timing/availability for the request (manually transitioned, or via\\n248. accepting a scheduling-proposal draft). Removed from the active priority queue view but\\n249. remains visible/filterable.\\n250. \\n251. ### 6.5 Done\\n252. Request/job has been completed or closed out (including declined/waitlisted outcomes).\\n253. Retained for reference, filterable, excluded from the default active queue view.\\n254. \\n255. ### 6.6 System States (apply across all of the above)\\n256. - **Empty:** No requests exist in a given view (e.g., a fresh demo reset, or the \\\"Done\\\"\\n257.   filter with nothing completed yet). Must show a clear, non-error empty message\\n258.   appropriate to the view (e.g., \\\"No new requests — simulate one to see triage in\\n259.   action\\\").\\n260. - **Loading:** Shown while simulated ingestion, parsing, or scoring is in progress (even\\n261.   if artificially/deliberately brief) so the UI never appears frozen or ambiguous.\\n262. - **Error:** Shown if a simulated parsing/scoring step fails for a given request (e.g., a\\n263.   malformed seed entry). The request should still be recoverable/visible (per FR-5),\\n264.   and the error state should be scoped to the affected request/card, not the whole\\n265.   dashboard, so one bad request doesn't block the rest of the queue.\\n266. \\n267. ---\\n268. \\n269. ## 7. Sample Seed Data Requirements\\n270. \\n271. Seed data must supply realistic, **messy** requests per trade, directly modeled on\\n272. `customer-research.md` §8 vignettes and §4 channel breakdown. At minimum, per trade:\\n273. \\n274. ### 7.1 Cleaner (Maria) seed set\\n275. - One **recurring-client, low-urgency** confirmation-style message (near-zero action\\n276.   needed) — e.g., a text confirming next week's regular clean.\\n277. - One **vague, incomplete lead** with no date given (e.g., voicemail: \\\"deep clean\\n278.   sometime this month,\\\" unknown caller).\\n279. - One **urgent, new-customer, tight-deadline** request via a lower-trust channel (e.g.,\\n280.   Instagram DM: move-out clean needed in ~2 days) — deliberately incomplete on address.\\n281. \\n282. ### 7.2 Handyman (Darnell) seed set\\n283. - One **urgent-sounding but unverified** voicemail from an unfamiliar name, vague\\n284.   severity, no address, no photo (mirrors Vignette B) — must exercise the urgency vs.\\n285.   completeness tension in Section 5.1/5.4.\\n286. - One **out-of-scope/service-fit** request (e.g., electrical panel work) to exercise\\n287.   Section 5.5.\\n288. - One **clear, well-scoped, recurring landlord/property-manager** job with full details,\\n289.   to contrast against the messy examples and show a high-completeness, high-value case.\\n290. \\n291. ### 7.3 Pet Sitter (Priya) seed set\\n292. - One **new-client booking-form submission**, multi-day request, missing pet temperament\\n293.   info — exercises completeness gap on a trade-specific critical field.\\n294. - One **loyal recurring client, short-notice, overlapping high-volume period** text\\n295.   request (mirrors the Bella/holiday vignette) — exercises customer-value vs. recency\\n296.   tension.\\n297. - A **volume-spike cluster** (multiple near-simultaneous requests within the same demo\\n298.   window) to demonstrate prioritization ordering behavior under load, consistent with\\n299.   the described holiday-week flood scenario.\\n300. \\n301. ### 7.4 Cross-cutting seed requirements\\n302. - Seed data must span at least the channel set from `customer-research.md` §4 (text,\\n303.   voicemail, email, social DM, booking form) across the combined set, not necessarily\\n304.   one of each per trade.\\n305. - At least one seed request per trade must have a scheduling conflict against a seeded\\n306.   existing booking, to exercise Section 5.3.\\n307. - At least one seed request across the set must fail/require an error-state or\\n308.   needs-info path deliberately, to validate Section 6.6.\\n309. \\n310. ---\\n311. \\n312. ## 8. Follow-Up Message Suggestion Behavior\\n313. \\n314. - Suggested messages are **always drafts requiring explicit owner review and action**\\n315.   before being marked sent — this is non-negotiable per research (`customer-research.md`\\n316.   §6, `marketing-research.md` §4.2, `business-proposal.md` §2 item 3) and is treated as a\\n317.   hard constraint, not a configurable setting.\\n318. - Draft content should vary by request state and gaps:\\n319.   - **Needs Info requests** → drafts should ask targeted clarifying questions for\\n320.     exactly the missing fields (e.g., address, timing, pet temperament) rather than a\\n321.     generic \\\"can you tell me more?\\\" — mirroring the specific re-typing fatigue pain\\n322.     point.\\n323.   - **Scheduling-conflict requests** → drafts should propose alternative times or\\n324.     transparently note limited availability rather than falsely confirming a slot.\\n325.   - **High-value/recurring, low-urgency requests** → drafts should be short\\n326.     acknowledgments (e.g., confirmations) requiring minimal owner edits.\\n327.   - **Poor service-fit requests** → drafts should politely decline or refer out rather\\n328.     than propose scheduling.\\n329. - The owner can edit, regenerate, or discard any draft. Marking a draft \\\"sent\\\" only\\n330.   updates the simulated request state (e.g., toward Scheduled or Done) — it does not\\n331.   transmit anything externally (see Section 9).\\n332. - Drafts should read in a plausible, individually-voiced tone appropriate to each\\n333.   persona's trade (e.g., Priya's messages may reference pet-specific detail; Darnell's\\n334.   may reference scope/photos), reinforcing the \\\"professional consistency without losing\\n335.   control\\\" value axis from the business proposal.\\n336. \\n337. ---\\n338. \\n339. ## 9. Prototype Constraints\\n340. \\n341. These constraints are explicit and binding for this prototype build:\\n342. \\n343. - **No real integrations.** The system does not connect to real SMS, email, voicemail,\\n344.   social DM, or booking-form providers. All inbound requests originate from seed data via\\n345.   simulated ingestion (Section 4.1).\\n346. - **No authentication.** There is no login, account system, or multi-tenant user\\n347.   management. The prototype presents a single owner's dashboard for demo purposes.\\n348. - **No payments.** No billing, subscription, or payment processing of any kind is\\n349.   implemented, referenced pricing hypotheses ($15–$40/mo) are business-planning context\\n350.   only and are not implemented as a feature.\\n351. - **Simulated ingestion only.** \\\"New\\\" requests entering the system are demo-triggered or\\n352.   scripted from seed data, never fetched from or delivered to a real external channel.\\n353. - **No autonomous message sending.** Consistent with Section 8, the system never\\n354.   transmits a message to a real customer; \\\"send\\\" is a simulated state transition only.\\n355. - **Single-location, single-operator scope.** No multi-location, multi-staff, or\\n356.   franchise management features are in scope.\\n357. - These constraints exist to keep the prototype focused on demonstrating the triage →\\n358.   prioritization → draft → dashboard value loop convincingly, without the cost, security\\n359.   surface, or complexity of production integrations — consistent with the \\\"demo-focused\\n360.   business case,\\\" not a production system, framing established in\\n361.   `business-proposal.md`.\\n362. \\n363. ---\\n364. \\n365. ## 10. Acceptance Criteria\\n366. \\n367. The prototype is considered complete and demo-ready when all of the following hold:\\n368. \\n369. 1. **AC-1 — End-to-end journey walkable per persona.** For each of the three personas\\n370.    (Maria, Darnell, Priya), at least one seeded request can be walked live through the\\n371.    full journey in Section 3: appears via simulated ingestion → shows parsed fields →\\n372.    shows a priority score/tier with explanation → appears correctly grouped on the\\n373.    dashboard → has a suggested follow-up draft → can be reviewed/edited/marked sent (or\\n374.    transitioned) by the owner.\\n375. 2. **AC-2 — Prioritization reflects all five factors.** The seed data includes at least\\n376.    one request pair where changing a single factor (e.g., urgency vs. customer value)\\n377.    visibly changes relative rank order, and the dashboard explanation text correctly\\n378.    attributes the rank to the relevant factor(s).\\n379. 3. **AC-3 — Needs-info flagging works.** At least one incomplete seeded request is\\n380.    correctly flagged with the specific missing fields, and its suggested draft asks\\n381.    specifically for those fields.\\n382. 4. **AC-4 — Scheduling conflict detection works.** At least one seeded request that\\n383.    conflicts with an existing booking is flagged as a conflict and does not silently\\n384.    present as confirmable.\\n385. 5. **AC-5 — Service-fit handling works.** At least one seeded request outside the\\n386.    operator's service scope is scored/handled distinctly (lower rank and/or a\\n387.    decline/refer-out draft) rather than treated like an in-scope job.\\n388. 6. **AC-6 — All five dashboard states are reachable.** New, Prioritized, Needs Info,\\n389.    Scheduled, and Done are all reachable through normal demo interaction (automatic\\n390.    transitions and/or explicit owner actions).\\n391. 7. **AC-7 — Empty, loading, and error states are implemented.** Each is visibly\\n392.    demonstrable (e.g., a fresh/reset view, a deliberate loading pause during\\n393.    ingestion/scoring, and a scoped error on a malformed seed request) without crashing\\n394.    the rest of the dashboard.\\n395. 8. **AC-8 — Drafts are never auto-sent.** No code path exists in the prototype that\\n396.    transmits or marks a message \\\"sent\\\" without an explicit owner-initiated action.\\n397. 9. **AC-9 — Explainability is visible.** Every prioritized request's card/detail view\\n398.    shows a human-readable reason summary referencing at least one of the five scoring\\n399.    factors, not just a bare numeric score.\\n400. 10. **AC-10 — Constraints honored.** No authentication flow, no payment flow, and no\\n401.     real external channel connection exists anywhere in the running prototype (verifiable\\n402.     by inspection — Section 9).\\n403. 11. **AC-11 — Reset/replay works.** The demo can be reset to a known starting seed state\\n404.     and re-run without requiring a fresh deployment.\\n405. \\n406. ---\\n407. \\n408. *Document type: Product specification for the Neighborhood Ops Concierge prototype.\\n409. (`confirmation`|`clarifying-question`|`decline`|`scheduling-proposal`), `body`,\\n70.     `status` (`draft`|`sent`), `history: string[]` (prior regenerated versions).\\n71.   - `ScoreFactor`: `{factor: 'urgency'|'customerValue'|'scheduling'|'completeness'|\\n72.     'serviceFit', delta: number, label: string}` (human-readable reason string per\\n73.     factor, e.g. \\\"Urgent language detected\\\").\\n74. - **Outputs (file):** `src/models/types.ts` (or `schema.py`/equivalent).\\n75. - **Acceptance checks:** Type-checks/compiles cleanly; every field referenced by FR-4,\\n76.   FR-6, FR-8, FR-9 in the product spec has a corresponding model field (manual checklist\\n77.   cross-reference).\\n78. \\n79. ### T1.2 — Parser field extraction contract\\n80. - **Depends on:** T1.1\\n81. - **Inputs:** Raw seed message text + channel + trade (from T1.3 seed set). Product spec\\n82.   §4.2 (FR-4, FR-5).\\n83. - **Outputs:** A documented function signature\\n84.   `parseRequest(rawText, channel, trade, customerLookup) -> ParsedFields` where\\n85.   `ParsedFields` includes: `customerNameGuess`, `isKnownCustomer`, `jobType`,\\n86.   `urgencySignals: string[]`, `requestedDateTime?: string`, `address?: string`,\\n87.   `tradeSpecificFields: Record<string,string>` (e.g. `petTemperament`, `photoProvided`),\\n88.   `missingFields: string[]`. This task only defines the contract/interface and a stub\\n89.   that always returns a valid (possibly all-missing) `ParsedFields` object — never throws.\\n90. - **Acceptance checks:** Calling the stub on an empty/garbage string returns a valid\\n91.   object with all fields marked missing rather than throwing (satisfies FR-5 \\\"must not\\n92.   crash the request\\\").\\n93. \\n94. ### T1.3 — Seed data: customers & bookings\\n95. - **Depends on:** T1.1\\n96. - **Inputs:** Product spec §2 (personas), §7.4 (cross-cutting requirements: scheduling\\n97.   conflict per trade).\\n98. - **Outputs:** `src/data/seed/customers.json` and `src/data/seed/bookings.json` with:\\n99.   - ≥3 known/recurring customers per trade (varying tenure, one explicitly flagged\\n100.     high-loyalty per §5.2 example: \\\"I know it's short notice but can you squeeze me in\\\").\\n101.   - ≥2 seeded existing bookings per trade on the demo calendar, timed so that at least one\\n102.     seed request (T1.4) collides with one of them (feeds FR-satisfying AC-4).\\n103. - **Acceptance checks:** JSON validates against T1.1 schema; at least one booking per\\n104.   trade exists within the time window used by the conflicting seed request in T1.4.\\n105. \\n106. ### T1.4 — Seed data: cleaner (Maria) request set\\n107. - **Depends on:** T1.1, T1.3\\n108. - **Inputs:** Product spec §7.1.\\n109. - **Outputs:** `src/data/seed/requests.cleaner.json` (raw message text + channel +\\n110.   customerId/null + intended `simulateAt` ordering) containing exactly the three required\\n111.   vignettes:\\n112.   1. Recurring-client, low-urgency confirmation text (near-zero action).\\n113.   2. Vague, incomplete lead — voicemail, \\\"deep clean sometime this month,\\\" unknown caller,\\n114.      no date.\\n115.   3. Urgent, new-customer, tight-deadline (~2 days) move-out clean via Instagram DM,\\n116.      deliberately missing address.\\n117. - **Acceptance checks:** Each entry has raw text written as a plausible real customer\\n118.   message (not a structured/pre-parsed form); entry #3 has no address string present in\\n119.   the raw text; entry #2 has no explicit date string present.\\n120. \\n121. ### T1.5 — Seed data: handyman (Darnell) request set\\n122. - **Depends on:** T1.1, T1.3\\n123. - **Inputs:** Product spec §7.2.\\n124. - **Outputs:** `src/data/seed/requests.handyman.json` containing:\\n125.   1. Product spec §5.1.\\n170. - **Outputs:** `scoreUrgency(parsed, context) -> {delta: number, label: string,\\n171.   raisesNeedsVerification: boolean}`. Must implement the caveat: unverified urgency from\\n172.   an unfamiliar contact (no address/photo/vague severity) raises the urgency delta **and**\\n173.   sets `raisesNeedsVerification = true`, which T2.6 must fold into `needsInfo`.\\n174. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: (a) explicit keyword (\\\"emergency\\\") + known customer →\\n175.   high positive delta, no verification flag; (b) explicit keyword + unknown customer + no\\n176.   address → high positive delta **and** `raisesNeedsVerification = true`; (c) no urgency\\n177.   language + far-future date → near-zero/negative delta.\\n178. \\n179. ### T2.2 — Customer value scoring function\\n180. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n181. - **Inputs:** `isKnownCustomer`, customer tenure/recurrence flag from `customers.json`,\\n182.   loyalty-context phrases in raw text. Product spec §5.2.\\n183. - **Outputs:** `scoreCustomerValue(parsed, customerRecord) -> {delta, label}`. Known/\\n184.   recurring high-value customers get a positive boost even with zero urgency language;\\n185.   new/unknown customers get neutral/reduced boost.\\n186. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: known recurring customer with a low-urgency\\n187.   confirmation message still receives a positive delta > 0; unknown customer with\\n188.   identical message text receives delta ≤ 0 (relatively lower), demonstrating value\\n189.   differentiation independent of urgency (feeds AC-2 factor-isolation requirement).\\n190. \\n191. ### T2.3 — Scheduling conflict scoring function\\n192. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n193. - **Inputs:** `parsed.requestedDateTime`, trade's `bookings.json` slots. Product spec §5.3.\\n194. - **Outputs:** `scoreScheduling(parsed, bookings) -> {delta, label, conflict?: {bookingId,\\n195.   note}}`. Overlapping request → negative/neutral delta **and** populated `conflict`\\n196.   object (never silently ranked high); clear conflict-free slot → small positive delta.\\n197. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test with a requested time inside a seeded booking window\\n198.   returns non-null `conflict` and does not return the maximum possible positive delta;\\n199.   unit test with a clearly free slot returns null `conflict` and a small positive delta.\\n200. \\n201. ### T2.4 — Completeness scoring function\\n202. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n203. - **Inputs:** `parsed.missingFields`, trade-specific required-field list (e.g. pet\\n204.   temperament for PET, photo/severity for HND). Product spec §5.4.\\n205. - **Outputs:** `scoreCompleteness(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, needsInfo: boolean,\\n206.   missingFields: string[]}`. Must cap (not zero out) score contribution — i.e. an urgent\\n207.   but incomplete request still has urgency delta applied elsewhere, but this function's\\n208.   own delta/cap prevents the composite from reaching the top tier while incomplete.\\n209. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: request missing address + timing → `needsInfo = true`,\\n210.   `missingFields` lists exactly those two fields, delta is negative or capped; fully\\n211.   complete request → `needsInfo = false`, delta ≥ 0.\\n212. \\n213. ### T2.5 — Service fit scoring function\\n214. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n215. - **Inputs:** `parsed.jobType`, trade's configured/seeded service-scope list (define a\\n216.   simple static scope list per trade, e.g. handyman excludes \\\"electrical panel\\\",\\n217.   \\\"licensed electrical\\\"). Product spec §5.5.\\n218. - **Outputs:** `scoreServiceFit(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, fit:\\n219.   'in-scope'|'out-of-scope'|'unclear'}`. Out-of-scope → substantial negative delta and\\n220.   `fit = 'out-of-scope'` (this flag is consumed directly by T3.4 to route to a\\n221.   decline/refer-out draft).\\n222. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: T1.5 entry #2 (electrical panel) → `fit =\\n223.   'out-of-scope'`, delta is the most negative of all test cases; an in-scope job type →\\n224.   `fit = 'in-scope'`, delta ≥ 0.\\n225. \\n226. ### T2.6 — Composite scorer & tier assignment\\n227. - **Depends on:** T2.1–T2.5\\n228. - **Inputs:** Outputs of all five factor functions for a given request. Product spec §5.6.\\n229. - **Outputs:** `computeScore(request, context) -> {score: number, tier:\\n230.   'high'|'medium'|'low', needsInfo: boolean, scoreBreakdown: ScoreFactor[]}`. Combines the\\n231.   five deltas (simple weighted sum — document the weights in code comments as a\\n232.   deliberately simple/explainable model, not a black box, per product spec framing);\\n233.   derives tier from score bands; sets `needsInfo` if completeness flags it OR urgency's\\n234.   `raisesNeedsVerification` is true; `scoreBreakdown` is the ordered list of non-trivial\\n235.   factor contributions with human-readable `label`s for direct dashboard display.\\n236. - **Acceptance checks:** (AC-9) breakdown always contains ≥1 entry referencing a real\\n237.   scoring factor, never just a bare number; (AC-2) running this against a matched pair of\\n238.   seed requests that differ only in urgency vs. customer-value produces a visibly\\n239.   different rank order and the breakdown correctly attributes it to the varied factor.\\n240. \\n241. ### T2.7 — Queue ranking & recalculation trigger\\n242. - **Depends on:** T2.6, T0.2\\n243. - **Inputs:** Full `requests[]` array in store; an event bus/hook for \\\"request added\\\" or\\n244.   \\\"request field edited.\\\" Product spec FR-6, FR-7.\\n245. - **Outputs:** `rankQueue(requests) -> Request[]` (sorted by tier then score) plus a store\\n246.   subscription/effect that re-invokes `computeScore` + `rankQueue` whenever a request is\\n247.   added or its fields (e.g., missing info filled in by owner) change.\\n248. - **Acceptance checks:** Adding a new seed request via simulated ingestion changes the\\n249.   sorted order without a page reload; manually editing a request's missing address field\\n250.   in the store triggers a re-score and the request's tier/rank updates.\\n251. \\n252. ---\\n253. \\n254. ## Phase 3 — Follow-Up Message Suggestion Engine\\n255. \\n256. ### T3.1 — Draft template set: clarifying-question drafts\\n257. - **Depends on:** T2.4 (needs `missingFields`)\\n258. - **Inputs:** `request.missingFields`, trade, persona voice guidance from product spec §2\\n259. Removed from the active priority queue view but\\n249. remains visible/filterable.\\n250. \\n251. ### 6.5 Done\\n252. Request/job has been completed or closed out (including declined/waitlisted outcomes).\\n253. Retained for reference, filterable, excluded from the default active queue view.\\n254. \\n255. ### 6.6 System States (apply across all of the above)\\n256. - **Empty:** No requests exist in a given view (e.g., a fresh demo reset, or the \\\"Done\\\"\\n257.   filter with nothing completed yet). Must show a clear, non-error empty message\\n258.   appropriate to the view (e.g., \\\"No new requests — simulate one to see triage in\\n259.   action\\\").\\n260. - **Loading:** Shown while simulated ingestion, parsing, or scoring is in progress (even\\n261.   if artificially/deliberately brief) so the UI never appears frozen or ambiguous.\\n262. - **Error:** Shown if a simulated parsing/scoring step fails for a given request (e.g., a\\n263.   malformed seed entry). The request should still be recoverable/visible (per FR-5),\\n264.   and the error state should be scoped to the affected request/card, not the whole\\n265.   dashboard, so one bad request doesn't block the rest of the queue.\\n266. \\n267. ---\\n268. \\n269. ## 7. Sample Seed Data Requirements\\n270. \\n271. Seed data must supply realistic, **messy** requests per trade, directly modeled on\\n272. `customer-research.md` §8 vignettes and §4 channel breakdown. At minimum, per trade:\\n273. \\n274. ### 7.1 Cleaner (Maria) seed set\\n275. - One **recurring-client, low-urgency** confirmation-style message (near-zero action\\n276.   needed) — e.g., a text confirming next week's regular clean.\\n277. - One **vague, incomplete lead** with no date given (e.g., voicemail: \\\"deep clean\\n278.   sometime this month,\\\" unknown caller).\\n279. - One **urgent, new-customer, tight-deadline** request via a lower-trust channel (e.g.,\\n280.   Instagram DM: move-out clean needed in ~2 days) — deliberately incomplete on address.\\n281. \\n282. ### 7.2 Handyman (Darnell) seed set\\n283. - One **urgent-sounding but unverified** voicemail from an unfamiliar name, vague\\n284.   severity, no address, no photo (mirrors Vignette B) — must exercise the urgency vs.\\n285.   completeness tension in Section 5.1/5.4.\\n286. - One **out-of-scope/service-fit** request (e.g., electrical panel work) to exercise\\n287.   Section 5.5.\\n288. - One **clear, well-scoped, recurring landlord/property-manager** job with full details,\\n289.   to contrast against the messy examples and show a high-completeness, high-value case.\\n290. \\n291. ### 7.3 Pet Sitter (Priya) seed set\\n292. - One **new-client booking-form submission**, multi-day request, missing pet temperament\\n293.   info — exercises completeness gap on a trade-specific critical field.\\n294. - One **loyal recurring client, short-notice, overlapping high-volume period** text\\n295.   request (mirrors the Bella/holiday vignette) — exercises customer-value vs. recency\\n296.   tension.\\n297. - A **volume-spike cluster** (multiple near-simultaneous requests within the same demo\\n298.   window) to demonstrate prioritization ordering behavior under load, consistent with\\n299.   the described holiday-week flood scenario.\\n300. \\n301. ### 7.4 Cross-cutting seed requirements\\n302. - Seed data must span at least the channel set from `customer-research.md` §4 (text,\\n303.   voicemail, email, social DM, booking form) across the combined set, not necessarily\\n304.   one of each per trade.\\n305. - At least one seed request per trade must have a scheduling conflict against a seeded\\n306.   existing booking, to exercise Section 5.3.\\n307. - At least one seed request across the set must fail/require an error-state or\\n308.   needs-info path deliberately, to validate Section 6.6.\\n309. \\n310. ---\\n311. \\n312. ## 8. Follow-Up Message Suggestion Behavior\\n313. \\n314. - Suggested messages are **always drafts requiring explicit owner review and action**\\n315.   before being marked sent — this is non-negotiable per research (`customer-research.md`\\n316.   §6, `marketing-research.md` §4.2, `business-proposal.md` §2 item 3) and is treated as a\\n317.   hard constraint, not a configurable setting.\\n318. - Draft content should vary by request state and gaps:\\n319.   - **Needs Info requests** → drafts should ask targeted clarifying questions for\\n320.     exactly the missing fields (e.g., address, timing, pet temperament) rather than a\\n321.     generic \\\"can you tell me more?\\\" — mirroring the specific re-typing fatigue pain\\n322.     point.\\n323.   - **Scheduling-conflict requests** → drafts should propose alternative times or\\n324.     transparently note limited availability rather than falsely confirming a slot.\\n325.   - **High-value/recurring, low-urgency requests** → drafts should be short\\n326.     acknowledgments (e.g., confirmations) requiring minimal owner edits.\\n327.   - **Poor service-fit requests** → drafts should politely decline or refer out rather\\n328.     than propose scheduling.\\n329. - The owner can edit, regenerate, or discard any draft. Marking a draft \\\"sent\\\" only\\n330.   updates the simulated request state (e.g., toward Scheduled or Done) — it does not\\n331.   transmit anything externally (see Section 9).\\n332. - Drafts should read in a plausible, individually-voiced tone appropriate to each\\n333.   persona's trade (e.g., Priya's messages may reference pet-specific detail; Darnell's\\n334.   may reference scope/photos), reinforcing the \\\"professional consistency without losing\\n335.   control\\\" value axis from the business proposal.\\n336. \\n337. ---\\n338. \\n339. ## 9. Prototype Constraints\\n340. \\n341. These constraints are explicit and binding for this prototype build:\\n342. \\n343. - **No real integrations.** The system does not connect to real SMS, email, voicemail,\\n344.   social DM, or booking-form providers. All inbound requests originate from seed data via\\n345.   simulated ingestion (Section 4.1).\\n346. - **No authentication.** There is no login, account system, or multi-tenant user\\n347.   management. The prototype presents a single owner's dashboard for demo purposes.\\n348. - **No payments.** No billing, subscription, or payment processing of any kind is\\n349.   implemented, referenced pricing hypotheses ($15–$40/mo) are business-planning context\\n350.   only and are not implemented as a feature.\\n351. - **Simulated ingestion only.** \\\"New\\\" requests entering the system are demo-triggered or\\n352.   scripted from seed data, never fetched from or delivered to a real external channel.\\n353. - **No autonomous message sending.** Consistent with Section 8, the system never\\n354.   transmits a message to a real customer; \\\"send\\\" is a simulated state transition only.\\n355. - **Single-location, single-operator scope.** No multi-location, multi-staff, or\\n356.   franchise management features are in scope.\\n357. - These constraints exist to keep the prototype focused on demonstrating the triage →\\n358.   prioritization → draft → dashboard value loop convincingly, without the cost, security\\n359.   surface, or complexity of production integrations — consistent with the \\\"demo-focused\\n360.   business case,\\\" not a production system, framing established in\\n361.   `business-proposal.md`.\\n362. \\n363. ---\\n364. \\n365. ## 10. Acceptance Criteria\\n366. \\n367. The prototype is considered complete and demo-ready when all of the following hold:\\n368. \\n369. 1. **AC-1 — End-to-end journey walkable per persona.** For each of the three personas\\n370.    (Maria, Darnell, Priya), at least one seeded request can be walked live through the\\n371.    full journey in Section 3: appears via simulated ingestion → shows parsed fields →\\n372.    shows a priority score/tier with explanation → appears correctly grouped on the\\n373.    dashboard → has a suggested follow-up draft → can be reviewed/edited/marked sent (or\\n374.    transitioned) by the owner.\\n375. 2. **AC-2 — Prioritization reflects all five factors.** The seed data includes at least\\n376.    one request pair where changing a single factor (e.g., urgency vs. customer value)\\n377.    visibly changes relative rank order, and the dashboard explanation text correctly\\n378.    attributes the rank to the relevant factor(s).\\n379. 3. **AC-3 — Needs-info flagging works.** At least one incomplete seeded request is\\n380.    correctly flagged with the specific missing fields, and its suggested draft asks\\n381.    specifically for those fields.\\n382. 4. **AC-4 — Scheduling conflict detection works.** At least one seeded request that\\n383.    conflicts with an existing booking is flagged as a conflict and does not silently\\n384.    present as confirmable.\\n385. 5. **AC-5 — Service-fit handling works.** At least one seeded request outside the\\n386.    operator's service scope is scored/handled distinctly (lower rank and/or a\\n387.    decline/refer-out draft) rather than treated like an in-scope job.\\n388. 6. **AC-6 — All five dashboard states are reachable.** New, Prioritized, Needs Info,\\n389.    Scheduled, and Done are all reachable through normal demo interaction (automatic\\n390.    transitions and/or explicit owner actions).\\n391. 7. **AC-7 — Empty, loading, and error states are implemented.** Each is visibly\\n392.    demonstrable (e.g., a fresh/reset view, a deliberate loading pause during\\n393.    ingestion/scoring, and a scoped error on a malformed seed request) without crashing\\n394.    the rest of the dashboard.\\n395. 8. **AC-8 — Drafts are never auto-sent.** No code path exists in the prototype that\\n396.    transmits or marks a message \\\"sent\\\" without an explicit owner-initiated action.\\n397. 9. **AC-9 — Explainability is visible.** Every prioritized request's card/detail view\\n398.    shows a human-readable reason summary referencing at least one of the five scoring\\n399.    factors, not just a bare numeric score.\\n400. 10. **AC-10 — Constraints honored.** No authentication flow, no payment flow, and no\\n401.     real external channel connection exists anywhere in the running prototype (verifiable\\n402.     by inspection — Section 9).\\n403. 11. **AC-11 — Reset/replay works.** The demo can be reset to a known starting seed state\\n404.     and re-run without requiring a fresh deployment.\\n405. \\n406. ---\\n407. \\n408. *Document type: Product specification for the Neighborhood Ops Concierge prototype.\\n409. Product spec §5.1.\\n170. - **Outputs:** `scoreUrgency(parsed, context) -> {delta: number, label: string,\\n171.   raisesNeedsVerification: boolean}`. Must implement the caveat: unverified urgency from\\n172.   an unfamiliar contact (no address/photo/vague severity) raises the urgency delta **and**\\n173.   sets `raisesNeedsVerification = true`, which T2.6 must fold into `needsInfo`.\\n174. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: (a) explicit keyword (\\\"emergency\\\") + known customer →\\n175.   high positive delta, no verification flag; (b) explicit keyword + unknown customer + no\\n176.   address → high positive delta **and** `raisesNeedsVerification = true`; (c) no urgency\\n177.   language + far-future date → near-zero/negative delta.\\n178. \\n179. ### T2.2 — Customer value scoring function\\n180. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n181. - **Inputs:** `isKnownCustomer`, customer tenure/recurrence flag from `customers.json`,\\n182.   loyalty-context phrases in raw text. Product spec §5.2.\\n183. - **Outputs:** `scoreCustomerValue(parsed, customerRecord) -> {delta, label}`. Known/\\n184.   recurring high-value customers get a positive boost even with zero urgency language;\\n185.   new/unknown customers get neutral/reduced boost.\\n186. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: known recurring customer with a low-urgency\\n187.   confirmation message still receives a positive delta > 0; unknown customer with\\n188.   identical message text receives delta ≤ 0 (relatively lower), demonstrating value\\n189.   differentiation independent of urgency (feeds AC-2 factor-isolation requirement).\\n190. \\n191. ### T2.3 — Scheduling conflict scoring function\\n192. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n193. - **Inputs:** `parsed.requestedDateTime`, trade's `bookings.json` slots. Product spec §5.3.\\n194. - **Outputs:** `scoreScheduling(parsed, bookings) -> {delta, label, conflict?: {bookingId,\\n195.   note}}`. Overlapping request → negative/neutral delta **and** populated `conflict`\\n196.   object (never silently ranked high); clear conflict-free slot → small positive delta.\\n197. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test with a requested time inside a seeded booking window\\n198.   returns non-null `conflict` and does not return the maximum possible positive delta;\\n199.   unit test with a clearly free slot returns null `conflict` and a small positive delta.\\n200. \\n201. ### T2.4 — Completeness scoring function\\n202. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n203. - **Inputs:** `parsed.missingFields`, trade-specific required-field list (e.g. pet\\n204.   temperament for PET, photo/severity for HND). Product spec §5.4.\\n205. - **Outputs:** `scoreCompleteness(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, needsInfo: boolean,\\n206.   missingFields: string[]}`. Must cap (not zero out) score contribution — i.e. an urgent\\n207.   but incomplete request still has urgency delta applied elsewhere, but this function's\\n208.   own delta/cap prevents the composite from reaching the top tier while incomplete.\\n209. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: request missing address + timing → `needsInfo = true`,\\n210.   `missingFields` lists exactly those two fields, delta is negative or capped; fully\\n211.   complete request → `needsInfo = false`, delta ≥ 0.\\n212. \\n213. ### T2.5 — Service fit scoring function\\n214. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n215. - **Inputs:** `parsed.jobType`, trade's configured/seeded service-scope list (define a\\n216.   simple static scope list per trade, e.g. handyman excludes \\\"electrical panel\\\",\\n217.   \\\"licensed electrical\\\"). Product spec §5.5.\\n218. - **Outputs:** `scoreServiceFit(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, fit:\\n219.   'in-scope'|'out-of-scope'|'unclear'}`. Out-of-scope → substantial negative delta and\\n220.   `fit = 'out-of-scope'` (this flag is consumed directly by T3.4 to route to a\\n221.   decline/refer-out draft).\\n222. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: T1.5 entry #2 (electrical panel) → `fit =\\n223.   'out-of-scope'`, delta is the most negative of all test cases; an in-scope job type →\\n224.   `fit = 'in-scope'`, delta ≥ 0.\\n225. \\n226. ### T2.6 — Composite scorer & tier assignment\\n227. - **Depends on:** T2.1–T2.5\\n228. - **Inputs:** Outputs of all five factor functions for a given request. Product spec §5.6.\\n229. - **Outputs:** `computeScore(request, context) -> {score: number, tier:\\n230.   'high'|'medium'|'low', needsInfo: boolean, scoreBreakdown: ScoreFactor[]}`. Combines the\\n231.   five deltas (simple weighted sum — document the weights in code comments as a\\n232.   deliberately simple/explainable model, not a black box, per product spec framing);\\n233.   derives tier from score bands; sets `needsInfo` if completeness flags it OR urgency's\\n234.   `raisesNeedsVerification` is true; `scoreBreakdown` is the ordered list of non-trivial\\n235.   factor contributions with human-readable `label`s for direct dashboard display.\\n236. - **Acceptance checks:** (AC-9) breakdown always contains ≥1 entry referencing a real\\n237.   scoring factor, never just a bare number; (AC-2) running this against a matched pair of\\n238.   seed requests that differ only in urgency vs. customer-value produces a visibly\\n239.   different rank order and the breakdown correctly attributes it to the varied factor.\\n240. \\n241. ### T2.7 — Queue ranking & recalculation trigger\\n242. - **Depends on:** T2.6, T0.2\\n243. - **Inputs:** Full `requests[]` array in store; an event bus/hook for \\\"request added\\\" or\\n244.   \\\"request field edited.\\\" Product spec FR-6, FR-7.\\n245. - **Outputs:** `rankQueue(requests) -> Request[]` (sorted by tier then score) plus a store\\n246.   subscription/effect that re-invokes `computeScore` + `rankQueue` whenever a request is\\n247.   added or its fields (e.g., missing info filled in by owner) change.\\n248. - **Acceptance checks:** Adding a new seed request via simulated ingestion changes the\\n249.   sorted order without a page reload; manually editing a request's missing address field\\n250.   in the store triggers a re-score and the request's tier/rank updates.\\n251. \\n252. ---\\n253. \\n254. ## Phase 3 — Follow-Up Message Suggestion Engine\\n255. \\n256. ### T3.1 — Draft template set: clarifying-question drafts\\n257. - **Depends on:** T2.4 (needs `missingFields`)\\n258. - **Inputs:** `request.missingFields`, trade, persona voice guidance from product spec §2\\n259.   (Maria/Darnell/Priya tone) and §8.\\n260. - **Outputs:** `draftClarifyingQuestion(request) -> MessageDraft` producing text that\\n261.   itemizes exactly the specific missing fields (e.g., \\\"Could you send the address and\\n262.   what day works best?\\\" not a generic \\\"can you tell me more?\\\"). Core User Journey\\n69. \\n70. The end-to-end journey the prototype must demonstrate, mapped to persona pain points:\\n71. \\n72. 1. **Inbound request arrives (simulated ingestion).** A message is generated from seed\\n73.    data representing a channel (text, voicemail transcript, email, social DM, or booking\\n74.    form), attributed to a trade (cleaner/handyman/pet sitter) and either a known or new\\n75.    customer.\\n76. 2. **Parsed.** The prototype extracts structured fields from the raw message: customer\\n77.    identity (known/new), stated or inferred urgency signals, job type/scope, requested\\n78.    timing, address/location (if present), and any explicit missing-info gaps.\\n79. 3. **Prioritized.** The parsed request is scored and ranked against the current queue\\n80.    using the five factors in Section 5, and assigned a priority tier and rank position.\\n81. 4. **Shown on dashboard.** The request appears in the owner's queue, tagged with its\\n82.    state (Section 6), priority tier, key parsed details, and any flagged missing\\n83.    information or scheduling conflicts.\\n84. 5. **Suggested follow-up drafted.** The system generates a candidate reply message\\n85. Prioritization Logic\\n156. \\n157. Prioritization makes the operators' existing informal mental checklist\\n158. (`customer-research.md` §7) explicit, consistent, and visible. Each request is evaluated\\n159. against five factors. Each factor contributes to a composite score; the composite score\\n160. determines rank order and priority tier. The scoring approach below is intentionally\\n161. simple and explainable rather than a black-box model, per the transparency requirement\\n162. in `business-proposal.md` §5.2.\\n163. \\n164. ### 5.1 Urgency\\n165. - **Signal sources:** explicit keywords (\\\"ASAP,\\\" \\\"emergency,\\\" \\\"today,\\\" \\\"flooding,\\\"\\n166.   \\\"leaking,\\\" \\\"urgent\\\"), requested timing proximity (e.g., \\\"need it tomorrow\\\" vs. \\\"sometime\\n167.   next month\\\"), and channel-implied urgency (a same-day voicemail reads differently than\\n168.   a booking form for three weeks out).\\n169. - **Effect on score:** Higher urgency raises the composite score and can promote a\\n170.   request above older but lower-urgency requests. Urgency is the most volatile factor —\\n171.   it can override recency of arrival.\\n172. - **Caveat modeled from research:** Unverified urgency from an unfamiliar contact (no\\n173.   address, no photo, vague severity — cf. Darnell's Vignette B) should raise urgency\\n174.   score but simultaneously raise a \\\"needs verification\\\" completeness flag, preventing\\n175.   a request from being ranked as top priority purely on unverified alarm language.\\n176. \\n177. ### 5.2 Customer Value\\n178. - **Signal sources:** known/recurring customer flag, relationship tenure/frequency (if\\n179.   present in seed data), and stated loyalty context (e.g., \\\"I know it's short notice but\\n180.   can you squeeze me in\\\").\\n181. - **Effect on score:** Known, recurring, high-value customers receive a positive score\\n182.   boost even absent urgency language, reflecting the research finding that operators\\n183.   implicitly prioritize trusted recurring clients over louder new leads\\n184.   (`customer-research.md` §7, item 6; §5, item 4). New/unknown customers receive a\\n185.   neutral or reduced boost until vetted.\\n186. \\n187. ### 5.3 Scheduling Constraints\\n188. - **Signal sources:** requested date/time vs. existing simulated bookings/calendar slots\\n189.   for that trade's demo calendar.\\n190. - **Effect on score:** A request that conflicts with an already-committed slot is flagged\\n191.   with a conflict indicator and its score is adjusted downward (or clearly marked as\\n192.   \\\"requires displacing another job\\\") rather than silently ranked high — directly\\n193.   countering the \\\"promising a slot before checking the calendar\\\" failure mode\\n194.   (`customer-research.md` §5, item 5; §6). A request with clear, conflict-free\\n195.   availability receives a small positive adjustment reflecting ease of fulfillment.\\n196. \\n197. ### 5.4 Request Completeness\\n198. - **Signal sources:** presence/absence of address, job scope, timing, and\\n199.   trade-specific critical fields (e.g., pet temperament for pet sitters, photo/severity\\n200.   detail for handymen).\\n201. - **Effect on score:** Incomplete requests are not ranked at the very top even if urgent,\\n202.   because they cannot yet be acted on — they are instead flagged **Needs Info** (see\\n203.   Section 6) and the missing fields are itemized. Completeness does not zero out a\\n204.   request's priority; it caps how high a request can rank until clarified, and directly\\n205.   drives what the suggested follow-up message asks for (Section 8).\\n206. \\n207. ### 5.5 Service Fit\\n208. - **Signal sources:** parsed job type vs. the operator's configured/seeded service scope\\n209.   (e.g., a handyman's electrical work outside comfort/license zone; a cleaning request\\n210.   requiring services Maria doesn't offer).\\n211. - **Effect on score:** Poor or unclear service fit reduces score substantially and may\\n212.   route the request toward a \\\"decline/refer out\\\" suggested draft rather than a\\n213.   scheduling draft, regardless of urgency or customer value.\\n214. \\n215. ### 5.6 Composite Scoring & Explainability\\n216. - Each request's dashboard card must show, at minimum, a short breakdown of which\\n217.   factors pushed its rank up or down (e.g., \\\"Urgent language detected,\\\" \\\"Existing\\n218.   client,\\\" \\\"Conflicts with 2pm booking,\\\" \\\"Missing address\\\"). This is a required\\n219.   transparency element, not optional polish — it exists specifically to preempt the\\n220.   \\\"why was this prioritized this way\\\" trust objection identified in the business\",\"timestamp_utc\":\"2026-07-15T02:42:24.1333860+00:00\"}},{\"sequence\":18,\"type\":\"tool.call\",\"payload\":{\"callId\":\"toolu_01EdbirfHr8QmCC62Mr7q9pw\",\"toolName\":\"view\",\"arguments\":{\"path\":\"/local-workspace/7a76b8db3fefcf2a/c1365ba0329a7d92c80f40b50080da1764f074ca/docs/planning/product-spec.md\",\"view_range\":[220,411]},\"timestamp_utc\":\"2026-07-15T02:42:27.5878490+00:00\"}},{\"sequence\":19,\"type\":\"tool.result\",\"payload\":{\"callId\":\"toolu_01EdbirfHr8QmCC62Mr7q9pw\",\"content\":\"220.   \\\"why was this prioritized this way\\\" trust objection identified in the business\\n221.   proposal.\\n222. - Priority tiers (for dashboard grouping) should be derived from score bands, e.g.\\n223.   **High / Medium / Low**, with **Needs Info** treated as an overlay flag that can apply\\n224.   to a request at any tier rather than a competing tier.\\n225. \\n226. ---\\n227. \\n228. ## 6. Dashboard States\\n229. \\n230. ### 6.1 New\\n231. Request has been parsed but not yet reviewed by the owner. Newly arrived (simulated)\\n232. requests default here before prioritization scoring is applied or immediately alongside\\n233. it.\\n234. \\n235. ### 6.2 Prioritized\\n236. Request has been scored and ranked; sits in the active queue ordered by composite score\\n237. within its tier (High/Medium/Low). This is the default \\\"working\\\" state for actionable\\n238. requests.\\n239. \\n240. ### 6.3 Needs Info\\n241. Overlay/flag state (may apply within New or Prioritized) indicating one or more required\\n242. fields are missing (address, scope, timing, trade-specific detail). Dashboard must\\n243. visually distinguish these from fully actionable requests and surface the specific\\n244. missing fields.\\n245. \\n246. ### 6.4 Scheduled\\n247. Owner has confirmed timing/availability for the request (manually transitioned, or via\\n248. accepting a scheduling-proposal draft). Removed from the active priority queue view but\\n249. remains visible/filterable.\\n250. \\n251. ### 6.5 Done\\n252. Request/job has been completed or closed out (including declined/waitlisted outcomes).\\n253. Retained for reference, filterable, excluded from the default active queue view.\\n254. \\n255. ### 6.6 System States (apply across all of the above)\\n256. - **Empty:** No requests exist in a given view (e.g., a fresh demo reset, or the \\\"Done\\\"\\n257.   filter with nothing completed yet). Must show a clear, non-error empty message\\n258.   appropriate to the view (e.g., \\\"No new requests — simulate one to see triage in\\n259.   action\\\").\\n260. - **Loading:** Shown while simulated ingestion, parsing, or scoring is in progress (even\\n261.   if artificially/deliberately brief) so the UI never appears frozen or ambiguous.\\n262. - **Error:** Shown if a simulated parsing/scoring step fails for a given request (e.g., a\\n263.   malformed seed entry). The request should still be recoverable/visible (per FR-5),\\n264.   and the error state should be scoped to the affected request/card, not the whole\\n265.   dashboard, so one bad request doesn't block the rest of the queue.\\n266. \\n267. ---\\n268. \\n269. ## 7. Sample Seed Data Requirements\\n270. \\n271. Seed data must supply realistic, **messy** requests per trade, directly modeled on\\n272. `customer-research.md` §8 vignettes and §4 channel breakdown. At minimum, per trade:\\n273. \\n274. ### 7.1 Cleaner (Maria) seed set\\n275. - One **recurring-client, low-urgency** confirmation-style message (near-zero action\\n276.   needed) — e.g., a text confirming next week's regular clean.\\n277. - One **vague, incomplete lead** with no date given (e.g., voicemail: \\\"deep clean\\n278.   sometime this month,\\\" unknown caller).\\n279. - One **urgent, new-customer, tight-deadline** request via a lower-trust channel (e.g.,\\n280.   Instagram DM: move-out clean needed in ~2 days) — deliberately incomplete on address.\\n281. \\n282. ### 7.2 Handyman (Darnell) seed set\\n283. - One **urgent-sounding but unverified** voicemail from an unfamiliar name, vague\\n284.   severity, no address, no photo (mirrors Vignette B) — must exercise the urgency vs.\\n285.   completeness tension in Section 5.1/5.4.\\n286. - One **out-of-scope/service-fit** request (e.g., electrical panel work) to exercise\\n287.   Section 5.5.\\n288. - One **clear, well-scoped, recurring landlord/property-manager** job with full details,\\n289.   to contrast against the messy examples and show a high-completeness, high-value case.\\n290. \\n291. ### 7.3 Pet Sitter (Priya) seed set\\n292. - One **new-client booking-form submission**, multi-day request, missing pet temperament\\n293.   info — exercises completeness gap on a trade-specific critical field.\\n294. - One **loyal recurring client, short-notice, overlapping high-volume period** text\\n295.   request (mirrors the Bella/holiday vignette) — exercises customer-value vs. recency\\n296.   tension.\\n297. - A **volume-spike cluster** (multiple near-simultaneous requests within the same demo\\n298.   window) to demonstrate prioritization ordering behavior under load, consistent with\\n299.   the described holiday-week flood scenario.\\n300. \\n301. ### 7.4 Cross-cutting seed requirements\\n302. - Seed data must span at least the channel set from `customer-research.md` §4 (text,\\n303.   voicemail, email, social DM, booking form) across the combined set, not necessarily\\n304.   one of each per trade.\\n305. - At least one seed request per trade must have a scheduling conflict against a seeded\\n306.   existing booking, to exercise Section 5.3.\\n307. - At least one seed request across the set must fail/require an error-state or\\n308.   needs-info path deliberately, to validate Section 6.6.\\n309. \\n310. ---\\n311. \\n312. ## 8. Follow-Up Message Suggestion Behavior\\n313. \\n314. - Suggested messages are **always drafts requiring explicit owner review and action**\\n315.   before being marked sent — this is non-negotiable per research (`customer-research.md`\\n316.   §6, `marketing-research.md` §4.2, `business-proposal.md` §2 item 3) and is treated as a\\n317.   hard constraint, not a configurable setting.\\n318. - Draft content should vary by request state and gaps:\\n319.   - **Needs Info requests** → drafts should ask targeted clarifying questions for\\n320.     exactly the missing fields (e.g., address, timing, pet temperament) rather than a\\n321.     generic \\\"can you tell me more?\\\" — mirroring the specific re-typing fatigue pain\\n322.     point.\\n323.   - **Scheduling-conflict requests** → drafts should propose alternative times or\\n324.     transparently note limited availability rather than falsely confirming a slot.\\n325.   - **High-value/recurring, low-urgency requests** → drafts should be short\\n326.     acknowledgments (e.g., confirmations) requiring minimal owner edits.\\n327.   - **Poor service-fit requests** → drafts should politely decline or refer out rather\\n328.     than propose scheduling.\\n329. - The owner can edit, regenerate, or discard any draft. Marking a draft \\\"sent\\\" only\\n330.   updates the simulated request state (e.g., toward Scheduled or Done) — it does not\\n331.   transmit anything externally (see Section 9).\\n332. - Drafts should read in a plausible, individually-voiced tone appropriate to each\\n333.   persona's trade (e.g., Priya's messages may reference pet-specific detail; Darnell's\\n334.   may reference scope/photos), reinforcing the \\\"professional consistency without losing\\n335.   control\\\" value axis from the business proposal.\\n336. \\n337. ---\\n338. \\n339. ## 9. Prototype Constraints\\n340. \\n341. These constraints are explicit and binding for this prototype build:\\n342. \\n343. - **No real integrations.** The system does not connect to real SMS, email, voicemail,\\n344.   social DM, or booking-form providers. All inbound requests originate from seed data via\\n345.   simulated ingestion (Section 4.1).\\n346. - **No authentication.** There is no login, account system, or multi-tenant user\\n347.   management. The prototype presents a single owner's dashboard for demo purposes.\\n348. - **No payments.** No billing, subscription, or payment processing of any kind is\\n349.   implemented, referenced pricing hypotheses ($15–$40/mo) are business-planning context\\n350.   only and are not implemented as a feature.\\n351. - **Simulated ingestion only.** \\\"New\\\" requests entering the system are demo-triggered or\\n352.   scripted from seed data, never fetched from or delivered to a real external channel.\\n353. - **No autonomous message sending.** Consistent with Section 8, the system never\\n354.   transmits a message to a real customer; \\\"send\\\" is a simulated state transition only.\\n355. - **Single-location, single-operator scope.** No multi-location, multi-staff, or\\n356.   franchise management features are in scope.\\n357. - These constraints exist to keep the prototype focused on demonstrating the triage →\\n358.   prioritization → draft → dashboard value loop convincingly, without the cost, security\\n359.   surface, or complexity of production integrations — consistent with the \\\"demo-focused\\n360.   business case,\\\" not a production system, framing established in\\n361.   `business-proposal.md`.\\n362. \\n363. ---\\n364. \\n365. ## 10. Acceptance Criteria\\n366. \\n367. The prototype is considered complete and demo-ready when all of the following hold:\\n368. \\n369. 1. **AC-1 — End-to-end journey walkable per persona.** For each of the three personas\\n370.    (Maria, Darnell, Priya), at least one seeded request can be walked live through the\\n371.    full journey in Section 3: appears via simulated ingestion → shows parsed fields →\\n372.    shows a priority score/tier with explanation → appears correctly grouped on the\\n373.    dashboard → has a suggested follow-up draft → can be reviewed/edited/marked sent (or\\n374.    transitioned) by the owner.\\n375. 2. **AC-2 — Prioritization reflects all five factors.** The seed data includes at least\\n376.    one request pair where changing a single factor (e.g., urgency vs. customer value)\\n377.    visibly changes relative rank order, and the dashboard explanation text correctly\\n378.    attributes the rank to the relevant factor(s).\\n379. 3. **AC-3 — Needs-info flagging works.** At least one incomplete seeded request is\\n380.    correctly flagged with the specific missing fields, and its suggested draft asks\\n381.    specifically for those fields.\\n382. 4. **AC-4 — Scheduling conflict detection works.** At least one seeded request that\\n383.    conflicts with an existing booking is flagged as a conflict and does not silently\\n384.    present as confirmable.\\n385. 5. **AC-5 — Service-fit handling works.** At least one seeded request outside the\\n386.    operator's service scope is scored/handled distinctly (lower rank and/or a\\n387.    decline/refer-out draft) rather than treated like an in-scope job.\\n388. 6. **AC-6 — All five dashboard states are reachable.** New, Prioritized, Needs Info,\\n389.    Scheduled, and Done are all reachable through normal demo interaction (automatic\\n390.    transitions and/or explicit owner actions).\\n391. 7. **AC-7 — Empty, loading, and error states are implemented.** Each is visibly\\n392.    demonstrable (e.g., a fresh/reset view, a deliberate loading pause during\\n393.    ingestion/scoring, and a scoped error on a malformed seed request) without crashing\\n394.    the rest of the dashboard.\\n395. 8. **AC-8 — Drafts are never auto-sent.** No code path exists in the prototype that\\n396.    transmits or marks a message \\\"sent\\\" without an explicit owner-initiated action.\\n397. 9. **AC-9 — Explainability is visible.** Every prioritized request's card/detail view\\n398.    shows a human-readable reason summary referencing at least one of the five scoring\\n399.    factors, not just a bare numeric score.\\n400. 10. **AC-10 — Constraints honored.** No authentication flow, no payment flow, and no\\n401.     real external channel connection exists anywhere in the running prototype (verifiable\\n402.     by inspection — Section 9).\\n403. 11. **AC-11 — Reset/replay works.** The demo can be reset to a known starting seed state\\n404.     and re-run without requiring a fresh deployment.\\n405. \\n406. ---\\n407. \\n408. *Document type: Product specification for the Neighborhood Ops Concierge prototype.\\n409. Clear, well-scoped, recurring landlord/property-manager job, full details (contrast\\n129.      case — high completeness, high value).\\n130. - **Acceptance checks:** Entry #1 raw text contains urgency language but omits address and\\n131.   any severity/photo detail; entry #2's job type must not be in the seeded handyman\\n132.   service-scope list (T2.4 depends on this); entry #3 has every field T1.2 extracts\\n133.   present in the raw text.\\n134. \\n135. ### T1.6 — Seed data: pet sitter (Priya) request set\\n136. - **Depends on:** T1.1, T1.3\\n137. - **Inputs:** Product spec §7.3.\\n138. - **Outputs:** `src/data/seed/requests.petsitter.json` containing:\\n139.   1. New-client booking-form submission, multi-day, missing pet temperament info.\\n140.   2. Loyal recurring client, short-notice, text request landing inside a seeded\\n141.      high-volume/holiday period.\\n142.   3. A **cluster** of ≥3 near-simultaneous requests (same/adjacent `simulateAt`) to\\n143.      demonstrate ranking under load.\\n144. - **Acceptance checks:** Entry #1's raw text has no mention of the pet's temperament;\\n145.   entry #2's `simulateAt`/requested date falls inside the \\\"volume spike\\\" window shared by\\n146.   the cluster in #3; the cluster contains at least one high-value and one lower-value\\n147.   customer to make ordering meaningfully visible.\\n148. \\n149. ### T1.7 — Seed data: cross-cutting coverage audit\\n150. - **Depends on:** T1.4, T1.5, T1.6\\n151. - **Inputs:** Product spec §7.4 (channel coverage, ≥1 conflict per trade, ≥1\\n152.   error/needs-info path).\\n153. - **Outputs:** A coverage checklist (code comment or small test file, e.g.\\n154.   `src/data/seed/__tests__/coverage.test.ts`) asserting programmatically over the combined\\n155.   seed set: all 5 channels appear at least once; each trade has ≥1 request whose\\n156.   `requestedDateTime` overlaps a booking in `bookings.json`; ≥1 request across the full\\n157.   set has a deliberately malformed/unparseable raw text field (empty string or garbled\\n158.   text) to drive the error-state path.\\n159. - **Acceptance checks:** Coverage test passes; failing it (e.g., temporarily removing a\\n160.   channel) causes a visible test failure — confirms the check is real, not vacuous.\\n161. \\n162. ---\\n163. \\n164. ## Phase 2 — Prioritization Engine\\n165. \\n166. ### T2.1 — Urgency scoring function\\n167. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n168. - **Inputs:** `ParsedFields.urgencySignals`, `requestedDateTime`, `channel`,\\n169.   `isKnownCustomer` (for the \\\"unverified urgency\\\" caveat). Product spec §5.1.\\n170. - **Outputs:** `scoreUrgency(parsed, context) -> {delta: number, label: string,\\n171.   raisesNeedsVerification: boolean}`. Must implement the caveat: unverified urgency from\\n172.   an unfamiliar contact (no address/photo/vague severity) raises the urgency delta **and**\\n173.   sets `raisesNeedsVerification = true`, which T2.6 must fold into `needsInfo`.\\n174. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: (a) explicit keyword (\\\"emergency\\\") + known customer →\\n175.   high positive delta, no verification flag; (b) explicit keyword + unknown customer + no\\n176.   address → high positive delta **and** `raisesNeedsVerification = true`; (c) no urgency\\n177.   language + far-future date → near-zero/negative delta.\\n178. \\n179. ### T2.2 — Customer value scoring function\\n180. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n181. - **Inputs:** `isKnownCustomer`, customer tenure/recurrence flag from `customers.json`,\\n182.   loyalty-context phrases in raw text. Product spec §5.2.\\n183. - **Outputs:** `scoreCustomerValue(parsed, customerRecord) -> {delta, label}`. Known/\\n184.   recurring high-value customers get a positive boost even with zero urgency language;\\n185.   new/unknown customers get neutral/reduced boost.\\n186. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit tests: known recurring customer with a low-urgency\\n187.   confirmation message still receives a positive delta > 0; unknown customer with\\n188.   identical message text receives delta ≤ 0 (relatively lower), demonstrating value\\n189.   differentiation independent of urgency (feeds AC-2 factor-isolation requirement).\\n190. \\n191. ### T2.3 — Scheduling conflict scoring function\\n192. - **Depends on:** T1.2, T1.3\\n193. - **Inputs:** `parsed.requestedDateTime`, trade's `bookings.json` slots. Product spec §5.3.\\n194. - **Outputs:** `scoreScheduling(parsed, bookings) -> {delta, label, conflict?: {bookingId,\\n195.   note}}`. Overlapping request → negative/neutral delta **and** populated `conflict`\\n196.   object (never silently ranked high); clear conflict-free slot → small positive delta.\\n197. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test with a requested time inside a seeded booking window\\n198.   returns non-null `conflict` and does not return the maximum possible positive delta;\\n199.   unit test with a clearly free slot returns null `conflict` and a small positive delta.\\n200. \\n201. ### T2.4 — Completeness scoring function\\n202. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n203. - **Inputs:** `parsed.missingFields`, trade-specific required-field list (e.g. pet\\n204.   temperament for PET, photo/severity for HND). Product spec §5.4.\\n205. - **Outputs:** `scoreCompleteness(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, needsInfo: boolean,\\n206.   missingFields: string[]}`. Must cap (not zero out) score contribution — i.e. an urgent\\n207.   but incomplete request still has urgency delta applied elsewhere, but this function's\\n208.   own delta/cap prevents the composite from reaching the top tier while incomplete.\\n209. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: request missing address + timing → `needsInfo = true`,\\n210.   `missingFields` lists exactly those two fields, delta is negative or capped; fully\\n211.   complete request → `needsInfo = false`, delta ≥ 0.\\n212. \\n213. ### T2.5 — Service fit scoring function\\n214. - **Depends on:** T1.2\\n215. - **Inputs:** `parsed.jobType`, trade's configured/seeded service-scope list (define a\\n216.   simple static scope list per trade, e.g. handyman excludes \\\"electrical panel\\\",\\n217.   \\\"licensed electrical\\\"). Product spec §5.5.\\n218. - **Outputs:** `scoreServiceFit(parsed, trade) -> {delta, label, fit:\\n219.   'in-scope'|'out-of-scope'|'unclear'}`. Out-of-scope → substantial negative delta and\\n220.   `fit = 'out-of-scope'` (this flag is consumed directly by T3.4 to route to a\\n221.   decline/refer-out draft).\\n222. - **Acceptance checks:** Unit test: T1.5 entry #2 (electrical panel) → `fit =\\n223.   'out-of-scope'`, delta is the most negative of all test cases; an in-scope job type →\\n224.   `fit = 'in-scope'`, delta ≥ 0.\\n225. \\n226. ### T2.6 — Composite scorer & tier assignment\\n227. - **Depends on:** T2.1–T2.5\\n228. - **Inputs:** Outputs of all five factor functions for a given request. Product spec §5.6.\\n229. - **Outputs:** `computeScore(request, context) -> {score: number, tier:\\n230.   'high'|'medium'|'low', needsInfo: boolean, scoreBreakdown: ScoreFactor[]}`. Combines the\\n231.   five deltas (simple weighted sum — document the weights in code comments as a\\n232.   deliberately simple/explainable model, not a black box, per product spec framing);\\n233.   derives tier from score bands; sets `needsInfo` if completeness flags it OR urgency's\\n234.   `raisesNeedsVerification` is true; `scoreBreakdown` is the ordered list of non-trivial\\n235.   factor contributions with human-readable `label`s for direct dashboard display.\\n236. - **Acceptance checks:** (AC-9) breakdown always contains ≥1 entry referencing a real\\n237.   scoring factor, never just a bare number; (AC-2) running this against a matched pair of\\n238.   seed requests that differ only in urgency vs. customer-value produces a visibly\\n239.   different rank order and the breakdown correctly attributes it to the varied factor.\\n240. \\n241. ### T2.7 — Queue ranking & recalculation trigger\\n242. - **Depends on:** T2.6, T0.2\\n243. - **Inputs:** Full `requests[]` array in store; an event bus/hook for \\\"request added\\\" or\\n244.   \\\"request field edited.\\\" Product spec FR-6, FR-7.\\n245. - **Outputs:** `rankQueue(requests) -> Request[]` (sorted by tier then score) plus a store\\n246.   subscription/effect that re-invokes `computeScore` + `rankQueue` whenever a request is\\n247.   added or its fields (e.g., missing info filled in by owner) change.\\n248. - **Acceptance checks:** Adding a new seed request via simulated ingestion changes the\\n249.   sorted order without a page reload; manually editing a request's missing address field\\n250.   in the store triggers a re-score and the request's tier/rank updates.\\n251. \\n252. ---\\n253. \\n254. ## Phase 3 — Follow-Up Message Suggestion Engine\\n255. \\n256. ### T3.1 — Draft template set: clarifying-question drafts\\n257. - **Depends on:** T2.4 (needs `missingFields`)\\n258. - **Inputs:** `request.missingFields`, trade, persona voice guidance from product spec §2\\n259.   (Maria/Darnell/Priya tone) and §8.\\n260. - **Outputs:** `draftClarifyingQuestion(request) -> MessageDraft` producing text that\\n261.   itemizes exactly the specific missing fields (e.g., \\\"Could you send the address and\\n262.   what day works best?\\\" not a generic \\\"can you tell me more?\\\"). Product spec §8.\\n283. - **Outputs:** `draftConfirmation(request) -> MessageDraft` — short acknowledgment\\n284.   requiring minimal edits (e.g., \\\"See you Tuesday at 10am as usual!\\\").\\n285. - **Acceptance checks:** Generated draft is under a defined short-length threshold (e.g.,\\n286.   ≤ 2 sentences) and contains no clarifying-question phrasing.\\n287. \\n288. ### T3.4 — Draft template set: decline / refer-out drafts\\n289. - **Depends on:** T2.5\\n290. - **Inputs:** `request.serviceFit === 'out-of-scope'`. Product spec §8.\\n291. - **Outputs:** `draftDecline(request) -> MessageDraft` — polite decline/refer-out text,\\n292.   never a scheduling proposal.\\n293. - **Acceptance checks:** For T1.5 entry #2 (electrical, out-of-scope), the generated draft\\n294.   contains decline/referral language and does not contain scheduling/confirmation\\n295.   language.\\n296. \\n297. ### T3.5 — Draft router & regeneration\\n298. - **Depends on:** T3.1–T3.4, T2.6\\n299. - **Inputs:** Scored/flagged request (needsInfo, conflict, tier, serviceFit).
