(clipboard icon).\\n125. - **Customer line**: name + known/new badge — known/recurring customers get a small\\n126.   \\\"Repeat client\\\" tag, directly surfacing the customer-value factor (§5.2).\\n127. - **Message snippet**: 1–2 line truncated excerpt of the raw inbound text/transcript, in\\n128.   quotes, so the owner sees real evidence, not just parsed fields.\\n129. - **Needs Info banner** (⚠, amber): only rendered when the overlay flag is set; lists the\\n130.   specific missing fields by name (address, timing, pet temperament, etc.) — never a\\n131.   generic \\\"incomplete\\\" label (§5.4, AC-3).\\n132. - **Scoring rationale block**: 2–4 short bullet lines, each prefixed with ↑ (raised rank)\\n133.   or ↓ (capped/lowered rank), each naming one of the five factors in plain language\\n134.   (§5.6, AC-9). This block is always visible on the card, not hidden behind a click — it\\n135.   is a first-class trust element, not a tooltip.\\n136. - **Scheduling conflict indicator**, when present, renders as a distinct red-outlined\\n137.   sub-row: `⛔ Conflicts with 2:00 PM booking (Ravi's cleanup)` — never silently omitted\\n138.   (§5.3, AC-4).\\n139. - **Service-fit flag**, when present, renders as: `\\uD83D\\uDEAB Outside service scope: electrical\\n140.   panel work` and visually de-emphasizes the card (reduced elevation/opacity) rather than\\n141.   styling it as a normal actionable job (§5.5, AC-5).\\n142. - **Two primary actions**: `View Details` (opens Job Detail) and `Review Suggested Reply`\\n143.   (opens Job Detail directly on the Follow-Up panel, scrolled/focused) — both drill into\\n144.   the same screen, just different anchor points, keeping the IA flat.\\n145. - **Overflow menu (⋮)**: manual state transition shortcuts (Mark Scheduled, Mark Done,\\n146.   Dismiss) without leaving the list, for fast one-handed triage (FR-16, FR-15).\\n147. \\n148. **List ordering:** grouped by state per §6, and within \\\"Prioritized,\\\" sub-grouped by tier\\n149. High → Medium → Low, each internally ordered by composite score descending. \\\"New\\\" items\\n150. that haven't yet been scored appear in their own group above \\\"Prioritized,\\\" in arrival\\n151. order, with a \\\"Scoring…\\\" transient loading affordance if scoring is still in progress\\n152. (§6.6 loading state, scoped to the card).\\n153. \\n154. ### 3.3 Job Detail (secondary screen)\\n155. \\n156. Purpose: full context + the review/edit/send workflow for the suggested message. Opens as\\n157. a right-side drawer/modal on desktop, a full-screen pushed route on mobile (§5).\\n158. \\n159. ```\\n160. ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\\n161. │ ← Back to Queue                                    [State: New ▾]    │\\n162. │                                                                       │\\n163. │ \\uD83D\\uDD34 HIGH PRIORITY · Rank #2 of 4                                      │\\n164. │ Jordan T. · New customer · via Text · 12 min ago                     │\\n165. │                                                                       │\\n166. │ ── Parsed Details ─────────────────────────────────────────────────  │\\n167. │  Trade/Job type:   Plumbing repair (handyman)                        │\\n168. │  Requested timing: \\\"ASAP\\\" (no specific date/time given)              │\\n169. │  Address:          — not provided —                                  │\\n170. │  Urgency signals:  \\\"ASAP\\\", \\\"leaking bad\\\"                             │\\n171. │  Completeness:     ⚠ Missing: address, preferred time window         │\\n172. │                                                                       │\\n173. │  Raw message:                                                        │\\n174. │  \\\"Hey is anyone available today?? pipe under my sink is leaking     │\\n175. │   bad need someone ASAP\\\"                                             │\\n176. │                                                                       │\\n177. │ ── Why This Rank ──────────────────────────────────────────────────  │\\n178. │  ↑ Urgent language detected (\\\"ASAP\\\", \\\"leaking\\\")            [High]    │\\n179. │  ↑ No conflict with existing schedule                      [Med]     │\\n180. │  ↓ Unverified — new contact, no address/photo provided      [Cap]    │\\n181. │  → Capped from Top rank pending verification (see Needs Info)        │\\n182. │                                                                       │\\n183. │ ── Suggested Follow-Up ────────────────────────────────────────────  │\\n184. │  Draft (asks for missing info — Needs Info request):                 │\\n185. │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │\\n186. │  │ Hi Jordan, thanks for reaching out! I can likely help today   │   │\\n187. │  │ or tomorrow. Could you send your address and a photo of the   │   │\\n188. │  │ leak, plus a good time window? That'll help me get you        │   │\\n189. │  │ scheduled quickly.                                             │   │\\n190. │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │\\n191. │  [ Edit Draft ]   [ Regenerate ]        [ Mark as Sent (simulated) ] │\\n192. │  ⓘ Sending is simulated — no message is transmitted to a real       │\\n193. │    customer in this prototype.                                       │\\n194. │                                                                       │\\n195. │ ── Manual State Actions ───────────────────────────────────────────  │\\n196. │  [ Mark Scheduled ]   [ Mark Done ]   [ Dismiss Request ]             │\\n197. └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\\n198. ```\\n199. \\n200. Section order is fixed and intentional: **Parsed Details → Why This Rank → Suggested\\n201. Follow-Up → Manual State Actions.** The owner reads context, understands the reasoning,\\n202. then acts on the message, then (optionally) overrides state manually. Rationale always\\n203. precedes the message draft so the owner isn't asked to trust a reply they haven't seen\\n204. justified yet.\\n205. \\n206. ### 3.4 Dashboard Summary/States Screen Variants\\n207. \\n208. - **Empty (e.g., fresh reset or \\\"Done\\\" filter with nothing yet):** centered illustration\\n209.   slot (optional) + message + a single primary action, e.g. *\\\"No new requests yet — tap\\n210.   'Simulate next message' to see triage in action.\\\"* Button links directly to the demo\\n211.   control in the top bar.\\n212. - **Loading (per card, during simulated ingestion/scoring):** the card renders in a\\n213.   skeleton/shimmer state with the channel icon and a \\\"Scoring…\\\" label instead of the\\n214.   rationale block; never a full-screen spinner that blocks the rest of the queue.\\n215. - **Error (per card, scoped):** card renders with a muted red left-border, a short\\n216.   message (*\\\"Couldn't fully parse this request — showing what we have\\\"*), and still\\n217.   shows any partially-parsed fields plus a `Needs Info` flag rather than disappearing\\n218.   (FR-5, §6.6).\\n219. \\n220. ---\\n221. \\n222. ## 4. Visual Hierarchy for Urgency/Priority Signals\\n223. \\n224. Priority communication must work through **shape + label + position**, not color alone\\n225. (color is a reinforcing signal, not the sole one, for accessibility):\\n226. \\n227. | Signal | Visual treatment | Notes |\\n228. |---|---|---|\\n229. | Priority tier (High/Med/Low) | Colored badge, top-left of card, always paired with text label (\\\"HIGH\\\", \\\"MEDIUM\\\", \\\"LOW\\\") | Red/Amber/Yellow-green; never rely on color chip alone |\\n230. | Rank within tier | Small `#N` next to tier badge | Numeric, always visible |\\n231. | Needs Info overlay | Amber ⚠ banner row, distinct from tier color | Overlay, not a competing tier — can appear on any tier per §5.6 |\\n232. | Scheduling conflict | Red-outlined sub-row with ⛔ icon | Always visible on card, never requires opening detail to discover |\\n233. | Service-fit issue | Reduced card elevation/opacity + \\uD83D\\uDEAB label | De-emphasized, not hidden — still auditable |\\n234. | Known/recurring customer | Small filled \\\"Repeat client\\\" tag next to name | Reinforces §5.2 without needing the rationale block |\\n235. | New/arriving request | Brief highlight pulse + \\\"New\\\" pill for ~10s after insertion | Supports FR-1 (visible arrival without reload) |\\n236. | Card ordering | Position in the list itself is a priority signal | Highest composite score in the highest tier always renders first |\\n237. \\n238. Overall visual weight ladder (heaviest to lightest): scheduling conflict > tier badge >\\n239. Needs Info overlay > service-fit de-emphasis > customer-value tag > channel/timestamp\\n240. metadata. This ordering ensures a scheduling conflict is never visually buried under a\\n241. tier color, which would risk the owner double-booking (§5.3 failure mode).\\n242. \\n243. ---\\n244. \\n245. ## 5. Responsive Layout Behavior\\n246. \\n247. ### Desktop (≥ 1024px)\\n248. - Two-pane layout available: Job Queue as a scrollable left/center list (60–65% width),\\n249.   Job Detail opens as a right-side slide-in drawer (35–40% width) that overlays without\\n250.   navigating away — the queue stays visible/scrollable behind a dimmed backdrop.\\n251. - Dashboard Summary renders as a single horizontal row of chips above the queue.\\n252. - Job Card renders all elements in the anatomy (§3.2) in full, two-column layout\\n253.   optionally used for rationale bullets vs. metadata.\\n254. \\n255. ### Tablet (600–1023px)\\n256. - Single-column Job Queue, full width. Job Detail opens as a centered modal (not a\\n257.   drawer) covering ~80% of viewport width, with a close (×) affordance.\\n258. - Dashboard Summary chips wrap to two rows if needed rather than truncating counts.\\n259. \\n260. ### Mobile (< 600px)\\n261. - Single-column, edge-to-edge Job Cards; Dashboard Summary chips become a horizontally\\n262.   scrollable strip (swipe, not wrap) to preserve one-handed reach.\\n263. - Job Card content is progressively condensed: rationale block shows a maximum of 2\\n264.   bullets by default with a \\\"Show all reasons\\\" expand toggle; the raw message snippet\\n265.   truncates to 1 line.\\n266. - Tapping a card (not just its buttons) opens Job Detail as a **full-screen route** (not\\n267.   a modal) with a `←` back affordance at the top — consistent with mobile-first,\\n268.   one-handed use (FR-15).\\n269. - Primary actions on the card (`View Details`, `Review Suggested Reply`) stack full-width\\n270.   instead of side-by-side to keep tap targets large.\\n271. - Job Detail's fixed section order is preserved, but \\\"Manual State Actions\\\" collapses\\n272.   into a bottom sticky action bar with icon+label buttons so it's reachable via thumb\\n273.   without scrolling to the bottom of a long detail view.\\n274. - The suggested-message textarea in Edit mode expands to fill available height with a\\n275.   sticky \\\"Save Draft\\\" / \\\"Cancel\\\" bar pinned above the mobile keyboard.\\n276. \\n277. Interaction Patterns: Reviewing, Editing, and Sending Suggested Messages\\n283. \\n284. This is the highest-trust interaction in the prototype and must never read as automatic\\n285. (FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, AC-8).\\n286. \\n287. 1. **View draft (default state):** the Suggested Follow-Up panel always opens in\\n288.    **read-only preview** mode — a static, clearly bordered \\\"draft\\\" box, visually distinct\\n289.    from an input field (subtle background tint, a \\\"Draft\\\" label chip above it).\\n290. 2. **Edit:** tapping `Edit Draft` converts the box into an editable textarea in place\\n291.    (no navigation away). While editing, the button row changes to `Save Draft` /\\n292.    `Cancel`. Canceling reverts to the last saved/generated draft text without side\\n293.    effects.\\n294. 3. **Regenerate:** tapping `Regenerate` replaces the draft text with a new candidate\\n295.    drawn from the same suggestion logic (varies by request state/gaps per §8), with a\\n296.    brief loading shimmer on the draft box only (not the whole panel). Previous draft is\\n297.    discarded — no version history required for the prototype scope. A toast confirms\\n298.    *\\\"New draft generated.\\\"*\\n299. 4. **Send (simulated):** `Mark as Sent (simulated)` is a distinctly styled button\\n300.    (primary color, but always paired with the persistent inline disclosure text: *\\\"Sending\\n301.    is simulated — no message is transmitted to a real customer in this prototype.\\\"*).\\n302.    This disclosure string appears every time the panel is shown, not just once, so no\\n303.    path exists in the UI where sending looks real (AC-8, AC-10).\\n304.    - Requires a single explicit tap — no auto-send, no send-on-navigate-away, no send\\n305.      tied to any automatic state transition.\\n306.    - On confirmation, the button becomes a disabled/checked state (`✓ Sent`), the draft\\n307.      box becomes locked/read-only, and the request's state visibly updates (e.g., toward\\n308.      Scheduled) per FR-9/FR-16, with a toast: *\\\"Marked as sent (simulated) — Jordan T.\\n309.      moved to Scheduled.\\\"*\\n310. 5. **Discard:** an owner can dismiss a draft/request entirely via `Dismiss Request`\\n311.    (Manual State Actions), moving it to Done without ever generating or sending a\\n312.    message — this path must remain equally easy to find as sending, to avoid biasing the\\n313.    owner toward action they didn't intend.\\n314. 6. **No destructive-by-default styling:** `Regenerate` and `Dismiss` never use the same\\n315.    visual weight/color as `Mark as Sent`, so the owner cannot mis-tap between \\\"send this\\\"\\n316.    and \\\"throw this away.\\\"\\n317. \\n318. ---\\n319. \\n320. ## 7. Priority communication must work through **shape + label + position**, not color alone\\n225. (color is a reinforcing signal, not the sole one, for accessibility):\\n226. \\n227. | Signal | Visual treatment | Notes |\\n228. |---|---|---|\\n229. | Priority tier (High/Med/Low) | Colored badge, top-left of card, always paired with text label (\\\"HIGH\\\", \\\"MEDIUM\\\", \\\"LOW\\\") | Red/Amber/Yellow-green; never rely on color chip alone |\\n230. | Rank within tier | Small `#N` next to tier badge | Numeric, always visible |\\n231. | Needs Info overlay | Amber ⚠ banner row, distinct from tier color | Overlay, not a competing tier — can appear on any tier per §5.6 |\\n232. | Scheduling conflict | Red-outlined sub-row with ⛔ icon | Always visible on card, never requires opening detail to discover |\\n233. | Service-fit issue | Reduced card elevation/opacity + \\uD83D\\uDEAB label | De-emphasized, not hidden — still auditable |\\n234. | Known/recurring customer | Small filled \\\"Repeat client\\\" tag next to name | Reinforces §5.2 without needing the rationale block |\\n235. | New/arriving request | Brief highlight pulse + \\\"New\\\" pill for ~10s after insertion | Supports FR-1 (visible arrival without reload) |\\n236. | Card ordering | Position in the list itself is a priority signal | Highest composite score in the highest tier always renders first |\\n237. \\n238. Overall visual weight ladder (heaviest to lightest): scheduling conflict > tier badge >\\n239. Needs Info overlay > service-fit de-emphasis > customer-value tag > channel/timestamp\\n240. metadata. This ordering ensures a scheduling conflict is never visually buried under a\\n241. tier color, which would risk the owner double-booking (§5.3 failure mode).\\n242. \\n243. ---\\n244. \\n245. ## 5. Responsive Layout Behavior\\n246. \\n247. ### Desktop (≥ 1024px)\\n248. - Two-pane layout available: Job Queue as a scrollable left/center list (60–65% width),\\n249. This disclosure string appears every time the panel is shown, not just once, so no\\n303.    path exists in the UI where sending looks real (AC-8, AC-10).\\n304.    - Requires a single explicit tap — no auto-send, no send-on-navigate-away, no send\\n305.      tied to any automatic state transition.\\n306.    - On confirmation, the button becomes a disabled/checked state (`✓ Sent`), the draft\\n307.      box becomes locked/read-only, and the request's state visibly updates (e.g., toward\\n308.      Scheduled) per FR-9/FR-16, with a toast: *\\\"Marked as sent (simulated) — Jordan T.\\n309.      moved to Scheduled.\\\"*\\n310. 5. **Discard:** an owner can dismiss a draft/request entirely via `Dismiss Request`\\n311.    (Manual State Actions), moving it to Done without ever generating or sending a\\n312.    message — this path must remain equally easy to find as sending, to avoid biasing the\\n313.    owner toward action they didn't intend.\\n314. 6. **No destructive-by-default styling:** `Regenerate` and `Dismiss` never use the same\\n315.    visual weight/color as `Mark as Sent`, so the owner cannot mis-tap between \\\"send this\\\"\\n316.    and \\\"throw this away.\\\"\\n317. \\n318. ---\\n319. \\n320. ## 7. Rules:
- `frustration.level = "not_assessed"` MUST have `score: null` and is used only when the evidence is insufficient.
- `none` means frustration was assessed and none was observed.
